newsitem.title: USA: Caspian pipeline signing seen on schedule in Dec.
newsitem.headline: Caspian pipeline signing seen on schedule in Dec.

text.p: The signing of a deal to bring Kazakh oil via pipeline from the Caspian Sea up through one of Russia's Black Sea ports will go ahead in December, despite demands for an equity stake by Russia's monopoly pipeline operator Transneft, oil company partners said.

"The negotiations have concluded successfully. Between now and December 6 there will be lawyers drawing up documents and there will be a signing ceremony in Moscow on December 6 finalizing the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) restructuring," Chevron Corp spokesman Mike Libby said Tuesday.
The project now involves 50 percent ownership by eight companies and 50 percent ownership by the three governments, Libby added.
The companies involved are Chevron, Russian LUKoil, Mobil Corp, Rosneft, Oman Oil Co, British Gas Plc, Agip SpA of Italy, and Kazakh Munaigaz and Oryx Energy Co.
Kazakhstan, Oman and Russia hold the remaining 50 percent.

Also Tuesday, Transneft spokesman Ravil Plyanin said in Moscow that the company wants to be a shareholder in the deal, adding that the oil companies have not sufficiently valued the pipeline operator's role.
He said it was premature to say all outstanding problems had been resolved, adding that Transneft would seek to persuade consortium members to reallocate equity stakes.

Negotiations over the landmark project, which will cost around $1.5 billion and allow the oil partners to bring oil in significant volume from the huge Tenqiz oilfield in Kazakhstan to world oil markets, have been long and convoluted.
CPC partners remained optimistic that the December target would be met, despite doubt expressed by various members of the group in Russia on Tuesday.
"We fully expect the ceremony to take place on (December) the sixth," said an official at one of the eight oil company partners.
"I would say we value (Transneft's) technical expertise because we intend to hire them as operator of the pipeline. But the equity issue is separate," the oil company official said.
